subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit III — Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
title: Atomic, Ionic & Van der Waals Radii: Contractions & Anomalies
topics: Covalent, Metallic & Van der Waals Radii Hierarchy (r_vdw > r_met > r_cov)
quickSummary: Atomic dimensions are defined by Covalent, Metallic, and Van der Waals radii (r_vdw > r_met > r_cov). Poor shielding by 4f electrons (Lanthanide Contraction) causes 4d ≈ 5d radii, while poor 3d shielding causes r(Ga) < r(Al).
summary: Master periodic trends in atomic/ionic radii, the 3d transition profile, Lanthanide contraction, Scandide contraction, and isoelectronic series.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 Atomic Radii Types & Hierarchy
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Atomic Radii Types & Hierarchy

summaryBox.title: Radii Hierarchy
summaryBox.takeaway: r_vdw > r_met > r_cov. Radii decrease across a period (Z_eff increases) and increase down a group (shell addition).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ATOMIC RADII TYPES

   COVALENT RADIUS             METALLIC RADIUS           VAN DER WAALS RADIUS

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Covalent Radius ($r_{\text{cov}}$)**: Half the equilibrium internuclear distance between two single-bonded identical atoms ($r_{\text{cov}} = d / 2$).
• **Metallic Radius ($r_{\text{met}}$)**: Half the internuclear distance between adjacent metal ions in a crystal lattice.
• **Van der Waals Radius ($r_{\text{vdw}}$)**: Half the equilibrium distance between non-bonded adjacent atoms of neighboring molecules in the solid state.

$$\mathbf{r_{\text{vdw}} > r_{\text{met}} > r_{\text{cov}}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Periodic Anomalies: Lanthanide & Scandide Contractions
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Periodic Anomalies: Lanthanide & Scandide Contractions
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **3d Transition Series Profile**:
• $\text{Sc} \rightarrow \text{Cr}$: Radii decrease (increasing $Z_{\text{eff}}$ dominates).
• $\text{Mn} \rightarrow \text{Ni}$: Radii remain nearly constant (3d electron shielding balances $Z_{\text{eff}}$ increase).
• $\text{Cu} \rightarrow \text{Zn}$: Radii increase slightly ($3d^{10}$ inter-electronic repulsions dominate).

2. **Lanthanide Contraction ($4f^{14}$ Shielding Failure)**: Intervening $14\ f$-electrons shield extremely poorly, increasing $Z_{\text{eff}}$ dramatically at the $5d$ series. Consequently, $4d$ and $5d$ elements possess nearly identical atomic radii:
$$\mathbf{r(\text{Zr}_{4d}) \approx r(\text{Hf}_{5d}) = 1.59\text{ \AA} \quad \vert \quad r(\text{Nb}_{4d}) \approx r(\text{Ta}_{5d}) = 1.46\text{ \AA} \quad \vert \quad r(\text{Mo}_{4d}) \approx r(\text{W}_{5d}) = 1.39\text{ \AA}}$$

3. **Scandide Contraction (Group 13 Anomaly)**: Gallium ($Z=31$) is preceded by $10\ 3d$-elements. Poor $3d^{10}$ shielding increases $Z_{\text{eff}}$ at Gallium, pulling its valence shell inward so that:
$$\mathbf{\text{Actual Group 13 Trend: } \text{B} < \text{Ga } (1.35\text{ \AA}) < \text{Al } (1.43\text{ \AA}) < \text{In} < \text{Tl}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.3 Ionic Radii & Isoelectronic Series
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.3 Ionic Radii & Isoelectronic Series
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Cation Radius**: Always smaller than parent atom ($r_{\text{cation}} < r_{\text{atom}}$) due to electron loss and increased $\frac{Z}{e^-}$ ratio.
• **Anion Radius**: Always larger than parent atom ($r_{\text{anion}} > r_{\text{atom}}$) due to increased electron repulsion and decreased $\frac{Z}{e^-}$ ratio.
• **Isoelectronic Series**: For species with identical electron counts ($10\ e^-$), ionic radius is inversely proportional to nuclear charge $Z$ ($r \propto 1/Z$):

$$\mathbf{\text{N}^{3-} (1.71\text{ \AA}) > \text{O}^{2-} (1.40\text{ \AA}) > \text{F}^- (1.33\text{ \AA}) > \text{Na}^+ (1.02\text{ \AA}) > \text{Mg}^{2+} (0.72\text{ \AA}) > \text{Al}^{3+} (0.54\text{ \AA})}$$

quickRevision: Lanthanide contraction causes Zr ≈ Hf, Nb ≈ Ta, Mo ≈ W.
Scandide contraction causes r(Ga) < r(Al) in Group 13.
Isoelectronic ionic radius: r ∝ 1/Z (N³⁻ > O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺).
